## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the safe operation and maintenance of the
laboratory autoclave for steam sterilization of glassware, media,
reagent water, and biohazardous waste. Autoclaving uses saturated
steam under pressure (typically 121 C at 15 psi for 15--30 minutes)
to achieve sterilization by denaturing proteins and nucleic acids in
microorganisms. In the EA Program, the autoclave is used to sterilize
equipment for microbiological analyses (e.g.,
[SOP-L305 Colilert](SOP-L305-colilert-quanti-tray.qmd)), to
decontaminate foreign soil samples
([SOP-L015](SOP-L015-foreign-soil-handling.qmd)), and to sterilize
waste before disposal.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of the laboratory autoclave in EA Program
  laboratories for sterilization of liquids, solids, glassware, and
  biohazardous waste
- **Does not apply to:** Dry heat sterilization (use muffle furnace or
  drying oven); chemical sterilization (e.g., bleach, ethylene oxide);
  filter sterilization (see [SOP-L114](SOP-L114-vacuum-filtration.qmd))
- **Location:** *TBD* (confirm autoclave location; shared facility or
  SGM)


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Authorize autoclave use, approve waste protocols |
| Lab Manager       | Schedule maintenance, verify biological indicators |
| Trained Personnel | Operate the autoclave per this SOP          |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Thermal/Pressure:** The autoclave operates at 121 C and 15 psi.
  Pressurized steam causes severe burns. Never attempt to open the
  door while the chamber is pressurized.
- **Scalding liquids:** Autoclaved liquids are superheated and can
  boil violently (bumping) when disturbed. Allow liquids to cool
  inside the chamber for at least 10 minutes after the cycle
  completes, and open the door slowly.
- **Glassware failure:** Cracked or starred glassware may shatter
  under pressure. Inspect all glassware before loading.
- **Biological:** Biohazardous waste must be contained in autoclave
  bags. Assume the exterior of bags is contaminated until the cycle
  is verified.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Heat-resistant gloves (autoclave gloves, rated for steam)
- [ ] Safety glasses or face shield
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

### Emergency Procedures

For steam burns, flush with cool running water for at least
20 minutes and seek medical attention. If the autoclave fails to
depressurize, do not force the door; shut off power and contact the
lab manager. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Laboratory autoclave (gravity or pre-vacuum) | Confirm model and location with lab manager |
| Autoclave-safe trays (stainless steel or polypropylene) | For containing loads |
| Autoclave bags (clear or orange, printed with biohazard symbol) | For waste sterilization |
| Autoclave tape (indicator tape)       | External indicator; changes color at 121 C |
| Biological indicator ampoules (e.g., *Geobacillus stearothermophilus* spore strips) | For periodic verification |
| Chemical integrator strips (Class 5)  | Internal indicator in each load |
| Aluminum foil                         | For covering flask openings    |
| Heat-resistant secondary containers   | For liquids (to contain boil-over) |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Pre-Use Inspection

1. Check the water level in the autoclave reservoir; refill with
   distilled or deionized water if below the minimum mark
2. Inspect the door gasket for cracks, brittleness, or debris; clean
   if needed
3. Verify that the drain screen/strainer is clear of debris
4. Ensure the pressure gauge reads zero and the chamber is at ambient
   temperature

### 6.2 Loading

1. Select the appropriate cycle for the load type:

   | Load Type        | Cycle             | Temperature | Time     | Notes                          |
   |:-----------------|:------------------|:------------|:---------|:-------------------------------|
   | Wrapped instruments, glassware | Gravity | 121 C | 30 min | Loosely pack for steam penetration |
   | Liquids (media, water) | Liquid / Slow exhaust | 121 C | 15--30 min | Leave caps loose or cover with foil; use slow exhaust to prevent boil-over |
   | Biohazardous waste | Gravity          | 121 C       | 60 min   | Double-bag in autoclave bags; do not seal bags tightly |
   | Foreign soil (SOP-L015) | Gravity     | 121 C       | 30 min   | Per SOP-L015 requirements      |

2. Place items in autoclave-safe trays. Do not overload; leave space
   for steam circulation.
3. For liquids: loosen caps or cover with foil. Place containers in a
   secondary tray to catch boil-over.
4. For waste bags: leave bags slightly open or use bags with
   steam-permeable patches. Place bags upright in a tray.
5. Place a chemical integrator strip inside the center of the load
   (the coldest point)
6. Apply autoclave indicator tape to the outside of each package or bag

### 6.3 Running the Cycle

1. Close and latch the autoclave door securely
2. Select the appropriate cycle (see table above)
3. Start the cycle and record the start time in the autoclave logbook
4. Monitor the temperature and pressure gauges during the initial
   pressurization to confirm normal operation
5. Do not leave the area until the autoclave has reached operating
   temperature and pressure

### 6.4 Unloading

1. When the cycle is complete, verify that the chamber pressure has
   returned to zero before opening the door
2. Crack the door open 1--2 cm and wait 2--5 minutes to allow residual
   steam to vent (prevents steam flash and liquid bumping)
3. Wearing autoclave gloves and face shield, open the door fully
4. Allow liquids to sit in the chamber for an additional 10 minutes
   after opening the door before removing
5. Remove trays using autoclave gloves; place on a heat-resistant
   surface away from foot traffic
6. Check the chemical integrator strip: it should show a complete
   color change indicating adequate steam exposure. If incomplete,
   the load must be re-processed.
7. Record the cycle completion time, temperature, pressure, and
   integrator result in the autoclave logbook

### 6.5 Waste Handling After Sterilization

1. After a successful waste cycle, seal the autoclave bags
2. Sterilized biohazardous waste can be disposed in the regular trash
   **only if** the institution's waste policy permits this and the
   biological indicator program confirms efficacy
3. Label the sealed bag with "Autoclaved" and the date
4. If the chemical integrator did not pass, do not dispose; re-run the
   cycle or contact the lab manager

### 6.6 Shutdown

1. After the final cycle of the day, drain the chamber if the
   manufacturer recommends it
2. Leave the door slightly ajar to allow the chamber to dry and
   prevent odor buildup
3. Wipe the door gasket with a damp cloth to remove debris


## 7. Verification and Quality Control

- **Chemical indicators:** Include a Class 5 integrator strip in every
  load. This confirms that the load reached the target temperature for
  the required duration.
- **Biological indicators:** Run a *Geobacillus stearothermophilus*
  spore test at least monthly (or per campus EH&S policy). Incubate
  the exposed ampoule per the manufacturer's instructions. A positive
  (growth) result means the autoclave failed; quarantine all loads
  processed since the last successful test and contact the lab manager.
- **Autoclave logbook:** Record every cycle: date, operator, load
  description, cycle type, temperature, pressure, duration, and
  indicator results.
- **Annual maintenance:** Schedule a professional inspection and
  calibration of the pressure gauge, safety valve, and temperature
  sensor at least annually.


## 8. Maintenance

| Task                                  | Frequency              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------|
| Check water level in reservoir        | Before each use        |
| Clean door gasket                     | Weekly                 |
| Clean drain screen/strainer           | Weekly                 |
| Run biological indicator test         | Monthly                |
| Professional inspection and calibration | Annually              |
| Replace door gasket                   | As needed (when cracked or leaking) |


## 9. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Successfully autoclaved biohazardous waste | Standard trash (if permitted by campus policy) |
| Failed autoclave loads (indicator did not pass) | Re-process or contact EH&S |
| Used chemical/biological indicator strips | Standard trash         |
| Autoclave water (drain)       | Drain (non-hazardous unless contaminated) |

## 12. Training Record

Before operating the autoclave independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Observe a trained operator run a complete cycle (loading through
   unloading and indicator verification)
4. Demonstrate proper loading for liquids and for waste (bag
   preparation, indicator placement, cycle selection)
5. Run one complete cycle under supervision with a passing chemical
   integrator result
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
